transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because... well, I just can't seem to keep my mind on my actual experiments anymore. It's becoming a real problem at the lab. 

Like, I'll be right in the middle of an important grant call or a safety meeting, and I'll notice something completely minor—like a pump vibration in the background, or a side comment from one of the students, or I'll just suddenly remember some odd peak in an old data spectrum. And that's it, my focus is gone. I'm suddenly off chasing that one tiny detail for hours. Meanwhile, the actual project—the thing everyone actually needs from me—just completely falls apart. I just can't seem to filter anything out right now.
Have you had distinct periods when your mood was unusually elevated or unusually irritable compared with your usual self?

Yes, I have. Um, for months now, I've felt almost... electrified. It's like the lab is finally moving at my speed for once. 

But on the flip side of that, I've been incredibly irritable. If someone questions my plan or, you know, asks me to just slow down a bit... I snap at them. I've been snapping a lot, actually. It's gotten to the point where I've noticed the students are just completely avoiding my office.
During these energized periods, have you felt rested despite sleeping less than usual?

Yes, absolutely. Um, most nights lately I'm only getting maybe two or three hours of sleep. I'll just crash on the couch in my office with my laptop still open. But the weird thing is, I don't feel tired at all. I wake up feeling completely sharp and just... ready to get back to work. It honestly just feels like sleeping is this inefficient interruption to everything I need to get done right now.
Have these energized periods caused you to become unable to function normally at work or in your daily life?

Yes, unfortunately. Um... it's gotten to the point where my department has actually had to step in on decisions I used to handle myself. Because I was missing priorities and... well, my scheduling got completely confused. And my supervision of the students has been really strained lately. It actually started putting the main project, and even some lab safety expectations, at real risk. So... yes, it's definitely made it hard to function normally at work.
During this energized period, have you heard or seen things that others could not, or believed things that others said were not true?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. Um... I definitely haven't seen or heard anything that wasn't actually there. And as for believing things that aren't true... no, I don't think so. I mean, my colleagues might think my timeline for the project is way too aggressive right now, but my plans are all based on actual data. So, no, nothing like what you're describing.
